Working in the Nxeon codebase at /opt/nxeon (Next.js App Router + Prisma, a Hostinger-clone VPS/hosting platform, Proxmox-based). The business just bought its first non-OVH physical server (Hetzner) and needs to add real multi-provider/multi-region support to the fleet. I need a precise, accurate map of how physical nodes and IP addresses are modeled and used TODAY before designing the change. Report with exact file:line references — this is pure fact-finding, do not propose a design yourself.

1. Find the `Node` model (or whatever represents a physical Proxmox host) in prisma/schema.prisma — every field, especially anything related to identity (name/hostname), location/region, provider, and how a `Server` (customer VM) row relates to it (foreign key name). Is there only ONE node row today, or does the schema already support multiple? Confirm by checking how many Node rows actually exist if you can find a way to check (or note that a DB query would be needed).

2. Find every place `lib/proxmox.ts` hardcodes a "the node" concept — specifically the `NODE` constant/`pve` client I recall exists, and `pveFor(conn: NodeConn)`. What does `NodeConn` look like — does it already take arbitrary connection details (host/port/token) per node, or is it hardcoded to one node's credentials via env vars? Read the full file if it's not too long, or at least every exported function and the top of the file.

3. Find how a NEW VM gets assigned to a specific physical node during provisioning — search for "node" selection logic in `lib/order.ts`, `worker/*.ts`, or wherever VM placement happens. Is node selection currently hardcoded to a single node, or is there already a capacity-based node-picking mechanism (I recall `lib/node-capacity.ts` exists)? Report its exact logic.

4. Find the IP pool / dedicated-IP model — `lib/dedicated-ip.ts` was mentioned in this session as OVH-specific (uses `ovh()`, `virtualMac`). Find the Prisma model backing "available/assigned dedicated IPs" (search for `DedicatedIp` or similar in prisma/schema.prisma) — every field, especially anything about provider/region/which node it belongs to. Does it already have a `nodeId` or region concept, or is it flat/global?

5. Find `lib/ovh.ts`'s full usage surface (I already know it does virtualMac-based failover IP attachment) — confirm exactly which files import from it, so I know every call site that assumes "the provider is OVH" implicitly.

6. Check for any existing "region" or "location" concept ANYWHERE in the schema or lib/ (e.g. on Server, on marketing pages, on pricing) — even if unrelated to nodes, so I know if a `Region` enum/string convention already exists I should reuse rather than invent a second one.

7. Check how SSH access to a node/server is modeled — is there a `Server.rootPasswordEnc`-style field for the NODE itself (not customer VMs), or does the app only ever SSH into individual guest VMs, never the physical host directly for anything beyond what's already scripted in scratchpad one-offs this session?

Report everything with exact file:line references and real field names/types. Do not design the solution — just the ground truth.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# =============================================================================
3	# Nxeon — onboard a fresh Proxmox VE host as a compute node
4	# =============================================================================
5	# Run this ON the new Proxmox host (as root). It idempotently preps everything a
6	# Nxeon compute node needs, then prints the exact values to paste into the admin
7	# "Add node" form (/admin/nodes/new). Re-running is safe: every step checks
8	# current state before changing anything.
9	#
10	# What it does:
11	#   1. Create a NAT bridge vmbrX bound to a per-node /24 (e.g. 10.20.N.1/24)
12	#   2. Enable IPv4 forwarding + a MASQUERADE rule for that subnet (append-only)
13	#   3. Create the NVMe + HDD storages matching the Node's storageNvme/storageHdd
14	#   4. Create the cloud-init snippets dir + the nxeon vendor snippet
15	#   5. Create a Proxmox API role + user + token with the privileges the platform
16	#      needs (documented pveum commands)
17	#   6. Build (or document copying) the cloud-init templates VMID 9000-9004
18	#   7. Print the Add-node form values (apiUrl, tokenId, tokenSecret, pveNode,
19	#      subnetPrefix, natChain, sshPort range, storages, publicIp)
20	#
21	# SAFETY:
22	#   - Never flushes the firewall. It only APPENDS its own MASQUERADE/FORWARD
23	#     rules and only if an identical rule is not already present.
24	#   - Never touches running VMs. Template builds skip any VMID that exists.
25	#   - Never destroys storage. `pvesm add` is skipped when the storage id exists.
26	#
27	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
28	# CROSS-HOST NETWORKING — IMPORTANT LIMITATION (read before deploying node #2)
29	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
30	# Each node NATs its OWN private /24 (10.20.N.0/24) behind its OWN public IP.
31	# This makes each node fully self-sufficient for provisioning, IP allocation and
32	# SSH DNAT — but it does NOT give VMs on different physical hosts a shared LAN.
33	#
34	#   * A VM on node-1 (10.20.0.x) CANNOT reach a VM on node-2 (10.20.1.x) over the
35	#     private network. They are separate NAT islands.
36	#   * The worker's iptables NAT chain (NXEON_FWD*) is rebuilt per-host from the
37	#     DB; it only manages forwards local to the host it runs on.
38	#
39	# If you need private east-west connectivity between VMs on different nodes you
40	# must lay an overlay/VPN over the public IPs — e.g. WireGuard mesh or a VXLAN
41	# fabric (Proxmox SDN "VXLAN zone") — and route the /24s across it. That is out
42	# of scope for this script; it is a deliberate, documented follow-up. For the
43	# common case (independent single-node VPS customers) per-node NAT islands are
44	# exactly what you want.
45	#
46	# Assumption: node #2 is a SEPARATE physical box with its own public IP, NOT a
47	# second NIC on the same L2 as node #1. If two nodes truly share L2 you would
48	# instead give them the SAME bridge/subnet and split the IP range — but this
49	# script assumes the separate-host model above.
50	# =============================================================================
51	set -euo pipefail
52	
53	# ---------- Parameters (flags override env) ----------------------------------
54	NODE_NUM="${NODE_NUM:-2}"           # ordinal; drives subnet + nat chain defaults
55	SUBNET_OCTET=""                     # third octet of 10.20.X.0/24 (default: NODE_NUM-1)
56	PUBLIC_IP="${PUBLIC_IP:-}"          # this host's public IPv4 (auto-detected if empty)
57	BRIDGE=""                           # vmbrX (default: vmbr1)
58	NVME_STORAGE="${NVME_STORAGE:-vmdata}"
59	HDD_STORAGE="${HDD_STORAGE:-vmdata-hdd}"
60	NVME_ZPOOL="${NVME_ZPOOL:-}"        # existing ZFS pool for NVMe storage (optional)
61	HDD_DIR="${HDD_DIR:-/tank/backup}"  # dir-backed HDD storage path
62	SNIPPETS_STORAGE="${SNIPPETS_STORAGE:-$HDD_STORAGE}"
63	TOKEN_USER="${TOKEN_USER:-nxeon@pve}"
64	TOKEN_NAME="${TOKEN_NAME:-platform}"
65	TOKEN_ROLE="${TOKEN_ROLE:-NxeonProvision}"
66	BUILD_TEMPLATES="${BUILD_TEMPLATES:-0}"   # 1 = build 9000-9004 here; 0 = document copying
67	SSH_PORT_START="${SSH_PORT_START:-20000}"
68	SSH_PORT_END="${SSH_PORT_END:-29999}"
69	
70	usage() {
71	  cat <<EOF
72	Usage: $0 [flags]
73	  --node-num N          Node ordinal (default 2). Sets defaults for subnet + nat chain.
74	  --subnet-octet N      Third octet of the /24 (default: node-num - 1, e.g. node 2 -> 1 -> 10.20.1.0/24).
75	  --public-ip IP        This host's public IPv4 (auto-detected if omitted).
76	  --bridge vmbrX        NAT bridge name (default vmbr1).
77	  --nvme-storage NAME   NVMe storage id (default vmdata).
78	  --hdd-storage NAME    HDD storage id (default vmdata-hdd).
79	  --nvme-zpool POOL     Existing ZFS pool to back the NVMe storage (zfspool). Optional.
80	  --hdd-dir PATH        Directory for the HDD (dir) storage (default /tank/backup).
81	  --build-templates     Build cloud-init templates 9000-9004 on this host.
82	  -h, --help            Show this help.
83	
84	Environment variables mirror the flags (NODE_NUM, PUBLIC_IP, BRIDGE, ...).
85	EOF
86	}
87	
88	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
89	  case "$1" in
90	    --node-num) NODE_NUM="$2"; shift 2 ;;
91	    --subnet-octet) SUBNET_OCTET="$2"; shift 2 ;;
92	    --public-ip) PUBLIC_IP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
93	    --bridge) BRIDGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
94	    --nvme-storage) NVME_STORAGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
95	    --hdd-storage) HDD_STORAGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
96	    --nvme-zpool) NVME_ZPOOL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
97	    --hdd-dir) HDD_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
98	    --build-templates) BUILD_TEMPLATES=1; shift ;;
99	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
100	    *) echo "Unknown flag: $1" >&2; usage; exit 1 ;;
101	  esac
102	done
103	
104	# ---------- Derived values ---------------------------------------------------
105	[[ -z "$SUBNET_OCTET" ]] && SUBNET_OCTET="$((NODE_NUM - 1))"
106	[[ -z "$BRIDGE" ]] && BRIDGE="vmbr1"
107	SUBNET_PREFIX="10.20.${SUBNET_OCTET}."
108	SUBNET_CIDR="10.20.${SUBNET_OCTET}.0/24"
109	GATEWAY_IP="10.20.${SUBNET_OCTET}.1"
110	if [[ "$NODE_NUM" -le 1 ]]; then
111	  NAT_CHAIN="NXEON_FWD"
112	else
113	  NAT_CHAIN="NXEON_FWD_N${NODE_NUM}"
114	fi
115	PVE_NODE="$(hostname)"
116	[[ -z "$PUBLIC_IP" ]] && PUBLIC_IP="$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
117	
118	log()  { echo -e "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
119	ok()   { echo -e "  \033[32m✓\033[0m $*"; }
120	warn() { echo -e "  \033[33m!\033[0m $*"; }
121	
122	require_root() { [[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]] || { echo "Run as root on the Proxmox host." >&2; exit 1; }; }
123	require_cmd()  { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing required command: $1" >&2; exit 1; }; }
124	
125	require_root
126	require_cmd pvesm
127	require_cmd pveum
128	require_cmd iptables
129	
130	log "Onboarding node #${NODE_NUM} — ${PVE_NODE} (${PUBLIC_IP})"
131	log "  subnet ${SUBNET_CIDR} via ${BRIDGE} (gw ${GATEWAY_IP}), NAT chain ${NAT_CHAIN}"
132	
133	# =============================================================================
134	# 1 + 2. NAT bridge + ip_forward + MASQUERADE
135	# =============================================================================
136	log "[1/7] NAT bridge ${BRIDGE} (${GATEWAY_IP}/24)"
137	if ip link show "$BRIDGE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
138	  ok "bridge ${BRIDGE} already exists — leaving it as-is"
139	else
140	  # Append an isolated (no physical port) NAT bridge to /etc/network/interfaces.
141	  # We do NOT reload all interfaces (that could disrupt the host); we bring up
142	  # just this bridge with ifup.
143	  if ! grep -qE "^\s*auto\s+${BRIDGE}\b" /etc/network/interfaces 2>/dev/null; then
144	    cat >>/etc/network/interfaces <<EOF
145	
146	# --- Nxeon node #${NODE_NUM} NAT bridge (added by onboard-node.sh) ---
147	auto ${BRIDGE}
148	iface ${BRIDGE} inet static
149	        address ${GATEWAY_IP}/24
150	        bridge-ports none
151	        bridge-stp off
152	        bridge-fd 0
153	        post-up   echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward
154	        post-up   iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s ${SUBNET_CIDR} ! -d ${SUBNET_CIDR} -j MASQUERADE
155	        post-down iptables -t nat -D POSTROUTING -s ${SUBNET_CIDR} ! -d ${SUBNET_CIDR} -j MASQUERADE
156	EOF
157	    ok "wrote ${BRIDGE} stanza to /etc/network/interfaces"
158	  fi
159	  ifup "$BRIDGE" 2>/dev/null || warn "ifup ${BRIDGE} failed — bring it up manually / on next reboot"
160	  ip link show "$BRIDGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "bridge ${BRIDGE} is up"
161	fi
162	
163	log "[2/7] IPv4 forwarding + MASQUERADE (append-only, never flush)"
164	# Persist ip_forward.
165	if ! sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward 2>/dev/null | grep -q ' = 1'; then
166	  sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 >/dev/null
167	fi
168	if [[ ! -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-nxeon-ipforward.conf ]]; then
169	  echo "net.ipv4.ip_forward=1" >/etc/sysctl.d/99-nxeon-ipforward.conf
170	  ok "persisted ip_forward via /etc/sysctl.d/99-nxeon-ipforward.conf"
171	else
172	  ok "ip_forward already persisted"
173	fi
174	# Idempotent MASQUERADE (in case the bridge already existed without our post-up).
175	if iptables -t nat -C POSTROUTING -s "$SUBNET_CIDR" ! -d "$SUBNET_CIDR" -j MASQUERADE 2>/dev/null; then
176	  ok "MASQUERADE for ${SUBNET_CIDR} already present"
177	else
178	  iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s "$SUBNET_CIDR" ! -d "$SUBNET_CIDR" -j MASQUERADE
179	  ok "appended MASQUERADE for ${SUBNET_CIDR}"
180	fi
181	# The worker owns the NXEON_FWD* DNAT chain; we do NOT create/populate it here.
182	# We only make sure iptables is not blocking forwarded traffic wholesale.
183	warn "SSH DNAT chain ${NAT_CHAIN} is created + maintained by nxeon-worker from the DB — not by this script."
184	
185	# =============================================================================
186	# 3. Storages (skip if the id already exists — never destroys data)
187	# =============================================================================

191	elif [[ -n "$NVME_ZPOOL" ]]; then
